entries.reason: its one required method, -writeToURL:error: (MLWritable.h:16-17), writes a model file back to disk; the port reads model protobufs (CoreML/RevenantMLProto.h declares revenant_ml_read and no writer), so the protocol is owed until the object that adopts it exists. The writer exists now: CoreML/RevenantMLWrite.c encodes the reader's document back to the container, and tests/backports/host/coreml-writer round-trips two system models byte for byte, the host reading the written files back with the descriptions of the originals. The adopter exists now: CoreMLUpdate13.m's RevenantMLWritableWrappedModel adopts it, and the update loop writes each snapshot through it. What is missing is the port's own declaration of the protocol: no toolchain header of this folder declares MLWritable, so the row stays owed. Measured on this host, none of the eight classes checked adopts the protocol (MLModel, MLUpdateContext, MLUpdateTask, MLMultiArray, MLModelDescription, MLModelConfiguration, MLPredictionOptions answer NO to class_conformsToProtocol), and MLModel does not respond to -writeToURL:error:; MLUpdateContext.h:27 types its model as MLModel<MLWritable>, which is a type qualifier, not an adoption
entries.effect: the protocol is not there: NSProtocolFromString answers nil, and a class cannot declare conformance to it. The training loop that uses it now exists in CoreMLUpdate13.m, so only the declaration is owed. The row stays absent rather than being rewritten with a sentence about iOS 6, which was never the question.
